story: An Indian king persecuted the Christian Church in his realm, a church founded by an apostle. Astrologers predicted that the king's own son would one day become a Christian, so the king had the young prince isolated from all outside contact and imprisoned. Despite this isolation, the prince met a hermit, a holy man, and converted to Christianity through him. The prince kept his new faith even in the face of his father's anger and attempts at persuasion. Eventually the king himself converted to Christianity, turned over his throne to his son, and retired to the desert to live as a hermit. The son, now king, later abdicated his own throne and went into seclusion together with his old teacher, the hermit who had converted him.
blind: A ruler in a certain land persecuted the religious community in his realm, a community founded by a traveling teacher. Diviners predicted that the ruler's own child would one day adopt the persecuted faith, so the ruler had the young heir isolated from all outside contact and confined. Despite this isolation, the heir met a solitary holy man and converted to the faith through him. The heir kept this new faith even in the face of the parent's anger and attempts at persuasion. Eventually the ruler himself converted to the faith, handed over rule to the child, and withdrew into the wilderness to live as a solitary holy man. The child, now ruler, later gave up rule as well and went into seclusion together with the old teacher who had converted him.
title: Barlaam and Josaphat
